problems.form_value: The experimental task prompt began '[With the assistance of ChatGPT,]' (p. 13).
problems.source_says: The PIT prompt begins on p. 12 with the Mattel scenario, which is the same in both arms. The bracketed text for the experimental condition opens the third and last paragraph of the prompt, the instruction sentence at the top of p. 13, not the prompt. arms[0].description words this correctly ('The task instructions added'). This is a detail error and does not touch criterion 1.
problems.quote: The adapted version featured a more complex scenario [square brackets indicate additional instructions for the experimental condition]: Mattel is an American toy manufacturer.
problems.locator: pp. 12-13, Measures, Creative problem-solving (PIT text: paragraphs 1-2 on p. 12, bracketed sentence at the top of p. 13)

confirmed.statement: (a) The document states random assignment: 'Male and female students who volunteered for the experiment were randomly assigned to either the control condition (task resolution without ChatGPT) or the experimental one (task resolution with ChatGPT) prior to the experiment.' The form's assignment quote is verbatim and its locator is right. This is the only passage on assignment, and it names no randomization mechanism.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Methods, Experimental Procedure, first full paragraph (checked on the page image)

confirmed.statement: The rest of the paper describes a true experiment. The abstract calls it a 'preregistered experiment' with 77 students with ChatGPT and 68 without, p. 9 gives the OSF preregistration, and the Limitations set the study's 'experimental nature' against 'Future quasi-experimental research'.
confirmed.locator: p. 2, Abstract; p. 9, end of Present Study; p. 26, Limitations and Future Directions

confirmed.statement: unit = individual is supported: the assignment sentence makes students the units assigned, before the experiment. The conditions then ran in separate sessions of at most five people ('The control group and experimental groups had separate sessions'), so session is confounded with condition. The paper does not say how sessions were scheduled. The form records this in open_questions[0].
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Experimental Procedure, first full paragraph; form open_questions[0]

confirmed.statement: structure = between is right: each student was in one condition. Table 1 heads its columns 'Control (N = 68)' and 'Experimental (N = 77)', Table 2 reports independent-samples t-tests with t(143), and the hypothesis tests are ANCOVAs with F(1,142).
confirmed.locator: p. 11, Table 1; p. 16, Table 2 and the text below it

confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is access to a generative-AI chatbot while each student produced his or her own PIT solutions: 'In the control condition, there were no other open tabs. In the experimental condition, the web browser had a second tab open with ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus).' Two experts blind to condition rated the answers that each participant produced, so the arms do not differ only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Experimental Procedure, second full paragraph; p. 13, Creative problem-solving

confirmed.statement: The treatment bundle in what_was_assigned and arms[0] matches the text. Before the PIT, the experimental condition got 'a brief description of ChatGPT with example prompts and responses' and three prompting tips, and it answered eight self-efficacy items (four without and four with ChatGPT) where the control answered four. The whole session took M = 36 minutes in the experimental arm and M = 26 in the control.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Experimental Procedure, fourth and fifth paragraphs; p. 13, Self-efficacy

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is generative AI: 'ChatGPT is an extension of a large language model (LLM) called GPT-3.5 or GPT-4 in its plus version'. name_model 'ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus)' is as printed. Because p. 4 ties the Plus version to GPT-4, the exact model is ambiguous, which does not affect (c). role = open_chat fits a free-use chatbot tab. Nowhere in pp. 1-40 does the paper report prompt logs or usage counts, only self-rated usefulness.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, ChatGPT subsection; p. 10, Experimental Procedure; p. 14, Perceived usefulness of ChatGPT; p. 16, Table 2 row 14

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arm matches the form (ai = none, ai_vs_bau). The control 'solved the second, complex ill-defined problem-solving task (Product Improvement Task; PIT) without the use of ChatGPT' in a single browser tab. Both arms could use the browser for other tools, but 'no one chose to do so', so neither arm used web search or another aid. The Figure 1 note repeats that the control solved the PIT without ChatGPT.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Experimental Procedure, second and third paragraphs; p. 17, Figure 1 note

confirmed.statement: (e) This is not a within-person AI design, so no order check applies. The Unusual Uses Task pre-test came first and 'without ChatGPT in both conditions'. The paper's 'within-subject differences' compare that pre-test with the later PIT, in a fixed order on two different tasks, not a randomized-order crossover. The form codes structure = between and uses the Figure 1 interaction only as a between-arm contrast of the change, which the randomization of arms supports.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Experimental Procedure, third paragraph; p. 17, Figure 1 note and the text below it

confirmed.statement: Counts: n_analyzed is 77 and 68 (145 in all), and 'no participants were excluded'. The paper prints no count at assignment, so arms[].n_randomized = null follows the form-spec rule on counts. The paper does not say whether any assigned volunteer failed to attend.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, first full paragraph; p. 11, Participants and Table 1; form-spec.md line 136, 'Counts in prose'

confirmed.statement: Balance fits random assignment. Table 1 shows no significant arm differences in gender, age, subject, study level, or prior ChatGPT experience. The closest is study level, chi2(1) = 2.76, p = .097 (13 vs 24 MA students). Baseline UUT originality is 1.74 vs 1.71 (p = .855). The 77/68 split is 0.75 binomial SD from an even split of 145 (exact two-sided p = .51 under a fair coin).

design_class = lab_rct and preregistered = yes are right: 'The experiment took place in a laboratory at the first author’s institution', and 'The experimental design and research hypotheses were preregistered at Open Science Framework (osf.io/q6wtu).'
confirmed.locator: p. 9, end of Present Study and Experimental Procedure

confirmed.statement: The candidate lead 'experiment_assignment_unclear' (the search report 'does not state the assignment method') does not hold for this document, which states random assignment on p. 10.
confirmed.locator: p. 10; candidates.json, c123 design_guesses and evidence

confirmed.statement: The file is the author accepted manuscript dated March 9th, 2024, and its title page says it is not the copy of record. Retrieval found no differences in studies or sample from the journal version, which I could not check.
confirmed.locator: p. 1, boxed notice; retrieval.json, c123 differences_from_latest

confirmed.statement: I read the whole document: pp. 1-23 in the markdown, pp. 2-4, 9-13, and 16-21 on the PDF page images, and pp. 23-40 (end of Discussion, Limitations, Conclusions, References, Appendix 1) in the PDF. No other passage bears on assignment.

summary: The PDF supports criterion 1: volunteers were randomly assigned, as individuals and before the sessions, to solve the Product Improvement Task with ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus) in a second browser tab (77 analyzed) or with no ChatGPT and, in practice, no other aid (68 analyzed), in a between-people design with no exclusions (pp. 10-11, 13). The one error is a detail in ai_tool.how_used, which says the experimental prompt 'began' with '[With the assistance of ChatGPT,]' when that phrase opens the prompt's last paragraph (pp. 12-13), and the separate sessions per condition, the unstated randomization mechanism, and the treatment bundle are risks of bias that the form already records.
